For your stir-fry, a good alternative to soy sauce that maintains the savory, umami flavor profile is coconut aminos. It is made from the sap of coconut blossoms and salt, making it soy-free and gluten-free. It has a slightly sweeter and milder taste than soy sauce, so you may want to add a splash of vinegar or a pinch of salt to balance the flavor. Another option is tamari if the person is only allergic to soy protein but not gluten, but since the allergy is to soy, coconut aminos is the safer bet. You can also use a mixture of mushroom broth and a little balsamic vinegar for a deep, savory note.
